object_description: T-shaped, very slender four-storey building with wrap-around balconies
geometry_property: outer layer of V-shaped steel girders
design_condition: the T-shaped volume is set back along the avenue to form a generous, address-forming access situation, allowing a second row of trees and following the contour of the neighbouring hall at the rear

positive: The project surprises with an unexpected urban planning approach
The T-shaped building creates a generous and address-forming access situation along the avenue
The opposite entrance area also benefits from this spatial widening of the street space
Reducing the footprint with a basement creates a four-storey building above ground
The recessed main wing allows a second row of trees and does not restrict the possible swimming pool location
In the transition to the neighbouring hall the new building follows its contour at a distance that guarantees exits, escape routes and lighting
A spacious square in front of the entrance can be enlivened by cafeteria and lecture hall, both rentable and publicly usable
Access to the building via the square is very spacious and the adjoining cafeteria enhances it as a meeting point
The direct entrances to the lecture hall and the sports and gymnastics hall are ideally located
The uses in the building are distributed very naturally, strengthening the public character of the entrance level
From the foyer the areas for students, staff and visitors are easily accessible via short routes
Generously designed corridors usable as work and study areas facilitate orientation
A meeting point for informal interaction is created at the transition from main staircase to corridor
The rhythm of storey-high glazing and cantilevered ceilings gives a very delicate horizontal emphasis
The high proportion of glass makes the building appear very open and inviting
The wrap-around balconies represent a high quality through spatial extension and additional lounge area
The building is very well organised and orientation works very well thanks to central access and bright corridors
The laboratory and patient area is complete and well organised with a good patient flow
Staff offices are sensibly arranged on the top floor
The sports hall is well developed and organised with a separate entrance for external use
The volume is the lowest of all projects examined and the design is generally very slender
The construction area is less than ten per cent of the floor area
negative: The outer layer of V-shaped steel girders appears somewhat elaborate and superimposed
The idiosyncratic column arrangement and the association with the tree avenues are less convincing
The recreational quality of the entrance square is still not very convincing
The row of pines is neither spatially nor atmospherically convincing and contradicts the avenue concept
Dissolving the chestnut avenue to the west seems incomprehensible
The garden courtyard does not have the character of a garden and its change of surface is not convincing
The proposed plant borders seem somewhat artificial in the context of the sports facilities
The truck access road does not seem practicable due to the lack of turning facilities
The concept of overlapping wings loses its urban clarity along one side and slightly exceeds the maximum height
The main entrance is not visible enough due to the uniformly continuous facade supports
The cardio fitness room is not on the same floor and the patient reception area is not shown
The proportions of the examination rooms are very unfavourable
The open-space offices cannot be converted into group offices in the desired number
Library and secretariat would have to be swapped and the library is not shown in full
The quality of the cafeteria outdoor space is not yet sufficiently evident and it is only partly suitable as a meeting place
The exclusively south-facing exposure is not balanced and requires permanent sun protection
Bicycle parking is hidden behind the building and should be better distributed
The proportion of glazing, the balconies and the used roofs are the cost drivers
Various urban and architectural aspects and the atmospheric quality of the open space are not entirely convincing
